body.statement: First resolve the legal kill-test slice \(d=1\), \(\kappa=0\), and \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma/(2\gamma+1)\): construct full-support priors on genuine i.i.d. Bernoulli laws in \(\mathcal P(1,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) whose values of \(\tau_P(0)\) attain the nuisance-dominated separation in \(\rho_{n,0}\) and whose fixed-\(n\) product mixtures have Hellinger distance bounded away from its testing maximum, or prove that the mixture handle cannot attain that separation and derive the replacement lower experiment that does. Conditional on passing this test, construct the corresponding same-class lower experiment in every primitive regime in which \(\rho_n/\rho_n^e\to\infty\), including unequal nuisance smoothness, noninteger corner powers, and max-norm tie surfaces, without deleting covariate support.
body.justification: The exact-class converse is the decisive novelty test because one-observation mixture cancellation does not control the shared-prior product experiment.
body.gap: Definition 1 and the Hellinger argument in KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE put zero design mass on nuisance-bump transition regions; RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009 requires a partition-local dependence structure that overlapping smooth frames do not satisfy verbatim.
body.consumer: A successful construction becomes a reusable lower-bound device for nonlinear causal functionals under known full-support random designs.

obligation.what_is_open: Bound the Hellinger or total-variation distance between the two fixed-\(n\) i.i.d. product mixtures at the nuisance-dominated separation, first for \(d=1\), \(\kappa=0\), and then in every claimed corner-zero regime, while keeping the covariate distribution exactly uniform and every component law inside the original H\"older class.
obligation.obstruction: Averaging the frame signs separately for each observation would prove equality, but that is not the experiment: one latent sign vector indexes the component law and is shared across all \(n\) observations. Consequently the two-observation expansion already contains nonzero overlapping terms involving products of frame signs. No dependency-graph, chi-square, or Hellinger expansion in the frozen core bounds their accumulated fixed-\(n\) contribution at the proposed separation. For \(\kappa>0\), baseline compensation additionally encounters noninteger corner cusps and max-norm tie nonsmoothness.
obligation.attempted: I verified the full-support squared-frame construction by expanding the three binary-cell-determining moments. This proves exact one-observation cancellation and legal target separation on the bounded-overlap kill-test slice. Expanding a product likelihood shows why the same calculation cannot be iterated: cross-observation terms retain the common signs. Treating the signs as freshly resampled would change the statistical experiment and is therefore invalid.
obligation.partial_result:
On the legal slice \(d=1\), \(\kappa=0\), choose a smooth bounded-overlap frame \(B_j\) with \(\sum_jB_j(x)^2=V(x)\), independent Rademacher signs \(\lambda_j\), and \(S_\lambda=\sum_j\lambda_jB_j\).  For constants \(p=3/8\), \(m=3/8\), \(t_0=1/8\), amplitudes \(a\asymp\ell^\alpha\), \(b\asymp\ell^\beta\), and \(\delta=2abV\), define
\[
 e_\lambda=p(1+aS_\lambda),\quad
 \mu_{0,\sigma,\lambda}=m+\sigma p\delta/2+\sigma(1-p)bS_\lambda,
 \quad \tau_\sigma=t_0-\sigma\delta/2.
\]
Small fixed amplitude constants put every component in the prescribed H\"older balls and interior intervals whenever \(\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\lesssim h^\gamma\).  Since \(\mathbb E_\lambda S_\lambda=0\) and \(\mathbb E_\lambda S_\lambda^2=V\), direct expansion gives
\[
 \mathbb E_\lambda e_\lambda=p,
 \quad
 \mathbb E_\lambda\{e_\lambda(\mu_{0,\sigma,\lambda}+\tau_\sigma)\}=p(m+t_0),
 \quad
 \mathbb E_\lambda\{\mu_{0,\sigma,\lambda}+e_\lambda\tau_\sigma\}=m+pt_0.
\]
These three moments determine the four probabilities of the binary pair \((A,Y)\), so the two one-observation mixtures coincide exactly and the contrast separation at zero is \(2ab\) when \(V(0)=1\).  This does not control the fixed-\(n\) product mixtures, because the same \(\lambda\) is shared by all observations and overlapping-frame cross-products survive from the second observation onward.
